section_summary: This section contains the first 80 pages of a U.S. consular report on Japan’s silk industry, with its contents, analysis, statistical tables, and charts. It examines cocoon farming, raw silk production and consumption, exports, foreign exchange, and the sharp rise in silk prices during 1939. Page 80 begins the discussion of government price and distribution controls; the report continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: The Status of Japan’s Silk Industry
subfiles.from: Vice Consul Ivan B. White, American Consulate, Yokohama
subfiles.about: A report on the agricultural, industrial, trade, and policy forces affecting Japan’s silk industry through 1939.
subfiles.summary: The report traces the contraction of sericulture after 1929 and its reversal when cocoon prices rose sharply in 1939. It compares raw silk production, reported domestic consumption, and exports, while questioning whether consumption figures include silk accumulated by weavers. Tables and charts document falling export volume, rising export value, silk’s importance to foreign exchange, and the effect of rayon and nylon competition. The section ends as the report begins to examine government purchases and controls.
